claims.text: The dynamic mechanical response of solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by a transition in the dominant plastic-deformation mechanism.
At lower temperatures and quasi-static strain rates, dislocation glide is the primary plastic-deformation mechanism in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Higher strain rates and/or elevated temperatures activate deformation twinning in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Higher strain rates and/or elevated temperatures can activate dynamic recrystallization in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Activation of twinning and/or dynamic recrystallization significantly increases strain-rate sensitivity.
Activation of twinning and/or dynamic recrystallization increases or otherwise alters work-hardening behavior.
The proposed mechanism transition maintains the strength–ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Rapid solidification can produce Co-free FeNiCrMn with a homogeneous microstructure and low defect variability.
Changing temperature and strain rate will produce measurable evolution in dislocation density, deformation-twin density, and recrystallized-grain formation.
Thermal activation and stress concentration trigger the proposed twinning and dynamic-recrystallization mechanisms.
Quasi-static room-temperature FeNiCrMn has relatively low strain-rate sensitivity.
The yield strength of Co-free FeNiCrMn becomes more sensitive to strain rate under dynamic loading.
Higher strain rates and/or elevated temperatures will increase twin density or the fraction of recrystallized regions in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The strain-hardening response of Co-free FeNiCrMn changes at higher strain rates and/or elevated temperatures.
Chemical inhomogeneity, pre-existing defects, oxidation, or other extrinsic effects may cause the proposed mechanism transition not to govern the measured response.
The threshold temperatures and strain rates for the proposed transition may vary with processing differences.
The hypothesis is falsified if the tested range shows neither activation of twinning or recrystallization nor a distinct transition in strain-rate sensitivity and work hardening.
